interstellar_medium.goal: A hot young star gives off Q ionising photons a second into gas of n atoms per cubic metre. Each ionised atom recombines at the rate n·α; write the radius R of the ball of gas the star can keep ionised.
interstellar_medium.name: Strömgren sphere
interstellar_medium.ask: Find R in parsecs for Q = 1e49 /s, n = 1e7 /m³, a = 2.6e-19 m³/s (one parsec p = 3.086e16 m).
interstellar_medium.method: Balance: every photon ionises one atom, and inside the sphere atoms recombine at n²α per volume. So Q = (4/3)πR³·n²α.

exoplanetology.goal: A planet of radius r crosses in front of its star, whose radius is R, and blocks part of its light. Write the fraction δ of the starlight that is lost, as a percentage.
exoplanetology.name: Transit depth
exoplanetology.ask: Find δ in per cent for a Jupiter-sized planet (r = 7.0e7 m) in front of the Sun (R = 6.96e8 m).
exoplanetology.method: The planet's disc blocks an area πr² of the star's disc πR².

accretion_physics.goal: Light from gas falling onto a mass M pushes on its electrons (cross-section σ) while gravity pulls on its protons (mass m). Write the luminosity L at which the two balance, using G and c.
accretion_physics.name: Eddington luminosity
accretion_physics.form: 4 * π * G * M * m * c / σ
accretion_physics.ask: Find L in units of 1e31 W (u = 1e31) for ten solar masses: M = 1.989e31 kg, m = 1.6726e-27 kg, c = 2.998e8 m/s, s = 6.652e-29 m², G = 6.674e-11.
accretion_physics.method: The radiation force on an electron at distance r is σL/(4πr²c); gravity on its proton is GMm/r². The r² cancels.

cosmic_web.goal: For the Universe to be exactly flat, the mass in each cubic metre must balance its expansion rate H against gravity's constant G. Write how much mass ρ each cubic metre must hold.
cosmic_web.name: Critical density
cosmic_web.ask: Find ρ in protons per cubic metre for H = 2.27e-18 /s (70 km/s/Mpc), G = 6.674e-11 and a proton mass m = 1.6726e-27 kg.
cosmic_web.method: Friedmann's equation, H² = 8πGρ/3 − k/a², with the curvature k set to zero.
